problems.title: Which DP?

parts.prompt: Count integers in [1, 10¹⁸] whose digits sum to 50:
For every node, the farthest distance to another node:

hints: Huge ranges → digits; every root → reroot.
problems.solution: Digit DP over 18 digits; rerooting in O(n).

problems.title: Rerooting
problems.solution: ans[0] = 8; moving to 2 brings 4 nodes closer and 2 farther: 8 − 4 + 2 = 6.

problems.title: Digit ones
problems.solution: 6 for 13; 21 for 100 (20 in 1–99, plus the 1 in 100).

problems.title: Distinct digits
problems.statement: Integers in [1, n] with no repeated digit.

problems.title: Tight flag
problems.statement: N = 352. You've placed the digits "3" and then "4".

options: No: 34 < 35, so the last digit is free (0–9)

hints: Tight while the prefix equals N's prefix.
problems.solution: Once a digit is below N's digit, every later digit is unconstrained.

problems.title: Leading zeros
problems.statement: Counting numbers with distinct digits, treating 007 as digits 0, 0, 7.
problems.solution: Leading zeros must not count as used digits.

problems.title: Range trick
problems.statement: Count numbers with property P in [L, R].

options: f(R) − f(L − 1) with f(x) = count in [0, x]
Run the DP twice with two tight flags only

problems.solution: The same prefix-difference idea as Part 1's prefix sums, applied to counts.

problems.title: Independent set on a tree
problems.statement: Path 1 – 2 – 3 – 4 with values [5, 1, 1, 5]; choose non-adjacent nodes, maximising the sum.

options: (best with v taken, best with v not taken)

problems.solution: Take the two ends: 10. The pair-returning contract is house robber III.
